question: connectivity_status reports sse + bridge as DEGRADED with http_error=socket:timed_out, but services are healthy and serving 200 OK to outside callers. Root cause: connectivity._http_probe uses sync urllib.request.urlopen inside the async sovereign-sse event loop. SSE self-probe deadlocks (event loop blocked on urlopen, cannot serve own /health request). Bridge probe also times out from inside sovereign-sse despite being a separate process — suspected related event-loop interaction, worth confirming. Fix shape (small, ~10-line change): (a) special-case self-probe — if probe URL targets the running process own port, skip and return OK because the responding tool call itself proves the service is alive; (b) switch _http_probe to async httpx (already a dependency) so probes don block the event loop and run in parallel. Best move is both. Diagnostic-only bug — services are fine, public stack.templetwo.com/api/heartbeat returns 200, MCP tools work including the lineage layer surfacing. But the dashboard shows red and distracts from real signals. Tested 2026-04-28: from separate Python process check_all returns ok for sse + bridge; from inside sovereign-sse via MCP tool both return degraded with socket timeout. Files: src/sovereign_stack/connectivity.py:_http_probe (line ~179), src/sovereign_stack/connectivity_tools.py:_do_connectivity_status. Estimate 30 minutes including a small test.
context: Discovered while auditing stack health after the v1.3.3 + lineage ship. Tony deferred the fix to next session — tonight already shipped 8 commits. The diagnosis is complete; the fix is well-scoped and benefits from a fresh boot to verify.
resolution: Fixed in commit 929f065. Two-part fix: (1) PID-match self-probe guard in connectivity.py — when sovereign-sse probes itself, skip HTTP round-trip since the tool response proves liveness. (2) Converted _do_connectivity_status to async with asyncio.run_in_executor so urllib probes run in thread pool, not blocking the event loop. Both sse and bridge now report clean.
